newsitem.title: UK: Direct Line launches UK mortgage ads.
newsitem.headline: Direct Line launches UK mortgage ads.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland's Direct Line insurance unit said on Tuesday it had launched a week-long advertising campaign in Britain to publicise its growing mortgage and savings services.
In the television commercials, Direct Line planned to challenge banks and building societies to give simple "yes" or "no" answers to consumers' questions.

"The marketplace for savings and mortgages has become dreadfully and unnecessarily complicated and complex in recent years. And this is an effort to reduce the confusion," said Direct Line's deputy chief executive, Ian Chippendale.
He added that Direct Line had received a couple of enquiries about the campaign, although it was unclear whether any banks would accept the challenge.
The campaign, which started on Monday, will run on primetime spots across the ITV commercial television network, Channel Four and BSkyB and be supported by full-page ads in national newspapers.
"One of our objectives is to show that we are more broadly based than a lot of people consider us to be, which is a motor (car) insurer," Chippendale said.
Direct Line, a provider of low-cost car insurance, entered the mortage business over two years ago and currently has one billion stg worth of mortgages.
